messages:
Alex: Heads-up — enterprise customer 'BrightLoop' opened a Sev-2. They see intermittent 502s from the API during heavy bursts, but our gateway should be returning 429 for quota hits. Support says it started ~10:30 PDT and reproduces with SDK bulk requests. filing here for triage.

Priya: Thanks Alex. Can you paste the customer repro steps / SDK call pattern? Also attach request IDs if available.

Alex: From support case:
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"input":"hello","max_tokens":50}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
They run with 200 concurrent requests. Response sample: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` with body `{"error":"quota-service unavailable"}`. Support attached trace-id headers: `x-request-id: rl-73a2ff` and a few `x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 10234` ms.

Mateo: Interesting — the body says `quota-service unavailable`. That suggests rate/quotas path is returning 5xx instead of the usual 429. Could be dependency timeout bubbling up. I want the envoy logs for one of those request IDs. Alex, can you paste a raw header set?

Alex: Provided two request IDs in the ticket: rl-73a2ff, rl-73b9cc. Support exported the gateway logs to the case, excerpt:  
```
[envoy] 2024-11-27T17:30:21Z "POST /v1/generate" 502 - via_upstream: quota-orch -> upstream_timeout
upstream_host: 10.12.34.56:8080
x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 10234
x-request-id: rl-73a2ff
```
Also a quota-orch stack trace: `Timeout waiting for policy-check response from quota-alloc (deadline exceeded)`

Jia: That aligns with a dependency hang. If quota-orch has a hard deadline configured, and the orchestrator returns 502 on upstream timeout, that would explain 5xx. We should confirm service behavior: should quota-orch map upstream timeouts to 429 or 502?

Priya: From product/contract: quota decisions must return 4xx on client exceed or policy denial. Internal dependency failures/timeouts need 5xx. But in this case the customer expectation is 429 for rate-limit exceeded. We must determine whether it's a misclassification (i.e., quota-orch timed out talking to allocator but the allocator *could* have said denial).

Sam: Running quick check on allocator health metrics — live dashboards show allocator p99 latency spiking to ~9s at the time window, and a small spike in connection errors. Could be a transient overload or an intermittent network flap to the allocator.

Nora: Also seeing an autoscale event on dedicated pools at the same time, which created a short flurry of control-plane retries. That might have interfered.

Mateo: Steps: 1) reproduce locally with controlled concurrency; 2) get full trace from the request id to see which hop timed out; 3) check quota-orch config mapping for upstream timeouts -> response code. I'll take 1 and 2. Jia, can you fetch config for quota-orch error mappings?

Jia: On it. quick grep shows in `quota-orch` error mapping:
```
// if allocator returns DENY -> 429
// if allocator returns TIMEOUT or UPSTREAM_ERROR -> 502
```
So behavior is intentional: allocator TIMEOUT -> quota-orch returns 502. That matches logs. But there is nuance: allocator should respond synchronously with DENY when policy exceeded. Timeouts shouldn't be common.

Alex: Support asks for an interim mitigation so customer doesn't see 5xx. They prefer we surface 429 for quota conditions even under partial allocator latency. Is that feasible?

Priya: We need to be careful — masking real backend failures as 429 could hide broader outages. Short term: route customers in affected tier to cached quota decisions or conservative deny-by-default logic to produce deterministic 429s when we can detect client exceeded rate. Long term: fix allocator HA and reduce tail latency.

Sam: For immediate mitigation: we can turn on `local-prefill` for quota-orch — it uses token-bucket local counters refreshed periodically, so it can answer 429 without allocator call for short windows. Ops: can we toggle config?

Nora: We can flip `local-prefill` on for the region and tier affected: `region-us-west-2, tier-enterprise`. Will need a config change and rollout. Estimated 8-12 min deploy with warmup. Do we want to proceed?

Alex: Customer has partial impact; support will offer temporary guidance if we can start deploy now. Go ahead if there are no blockers.

Jia: Also opened an infra ticket to increase allocator connection pool and add retry-attempts with jitter to reduce timeouts. We'll track that as follow-up.

Mateo: Repro notes from my local run (reproduced with our internal key): with 200 concurrent POSTs to `/v1/generate` we saw ~15% 502s when allocator p99 >= 8s. Envoy shows upstream timeout at 10s; quota-orch timed out at 9s and returned 502. Logs: `quota-orch: Allocator call timed out after 9s, returning 502`

Sam: Good repro. Can you capture a full trace for one of those failures? Use `x-trace-id` header and send to `ingest-traces` service.

Mateo: Sent one trace id `trace-rl-0001` to SRE tracing. Link: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/trace-rl-0001 (internal)

Priya: Action list so far:
- [ ] Ops: toggle `local-prefill` for region us-west-2 / tier enterprise (Nora) — ETA 12m
- [ ] Infra: increase allocator pool + retry config (Jia) — ETA 24h
- [ ] Runtime: add metric/alert for allocator timeouts mapping to quota-orch 5xx (Mateo) — ETA 6h
- [ ] Support: inform BrightLoop of interim mitigation + run customer-side backoff guidance (Alex) — ETA 30m

Nora: Starting deploy now. I'll post progress.

ops-bot: Deploy started by Nora: config-quota-orch-localprefill -> version v2024.11.3; rolling to us-west-2.

Nora: Canary ok for first 2 nodes, increasing to 10%. No errors so far.

Alex: Support updated BrightLoop: "We're enabling a short-term local quota evaluation for your region to reduce 5xx. Please retry with exponential backoff; we will follow up with a permanent fix." Customer replied: :thumbsup: and asked for ETA on root cause.

Mateo: Canary at 50% — latency for allocator calls dropped 60% on canary path and we're seeing 429s instead of 502 for the same client pattern.

ops-bot: Canary complete. Rolling to remaining nodes.

Nora: Rollout done in 11m. Confirming metrics: downstream 502s for BrightLoop are back to baseline; 429s increased as expected.

Priya: Great. Next steps: run allocator scaling test, add circuit-breaker to fail-fast to local counters sooner, and revisit mapping policy (product) to see if we should map allocator timeouts to 429 under specific conditions. I'll schedule a product + infra sync tomorrow.

Sam: Will add a Grafana panel for `quota-orch.upstream_timeout_rate` and alert when > 0.5% over 5m.

Alex: Closing loop on the ticket and flagging follow-ups. Logging case notes: cause = allocator tail latency + control-plane churn; immediate mitigation = local-prefill toggle; next fix = allocator pool/retry, circuit-breaker changes.

support-bot: Case #BR-4823 updated: mitigation applied, customer notified.

Jia: I'll keep infra ticket open and post allocator connection pool PR link once ready.

Alex: Thanks everyone — great cross-team response. If any regression, ping this thread.
